## The thirteenth day before the Kalends · 17 February

[0769]

In Persis, in the city of Babylon, the birthday of blessed Polochronius, bishop and martyr, who, in the presence of Decius the persecutor, struck on the mouth with stones, his hands stretched out, lifting his eyes to heaven, sent forth his spirit. At the city of Concordia, the passion of the saints Donatus, Secundianus, Romulus, with eighty-six others. In Scotia, of Saint Fintanus, presbyter and confessor, a man of great virtue. On this same day, of Saint Silvinus, bishop *Taruanensis*. [In Bouillart: . . . a man of great virtue. On this same day, of Saint Silvinus, bishop of the city of Toulouse.]

## The twelfth day before the Kalends · 18 February

[0773]

The birthday of blessed Simeon, bishop and martyr, who is known to have been a kinsman of the Saviour according to the flesh, and the son of Cleophas, who was the brother of Joseph. He, ordained bishop of Jerusalem after James the brother of the Lord, in the persecution of Trajan, afflicted with punishments for a long time, was consummated by martyrdom. All who were present, and the judge himself, marvelling that an old man of a hundred and twenty years had endured the punishment of the cross. In the city of Ostia, of the holy martyrs Maximus, Claudius and his wife Prepedigna with two sons, who, since they were of a most illustrious family, were seized at the command of Diocletian, and deported into exile; then, burned in a fire, they rendered to God the sweet-smelling sacrifice of martyrdom.

## The eleventh day before the Kalends · 19 February

[0777]

At Rome, the birthday of Saint Gabinius, presbyter and martyr, who, long afflicted with chains in custody by Diocletian, purchased the joys of heaven by a precious death. In Africa, of the saints Publius and Julian.

## The tenth day before the Kalends · 20 February

[0779]

At the city of Tyre, of the blessed martyrs, whose number the knowledge of God alone gathers. Who, at the command of Diocletian, were slain by many punishments of torments succeeding one another. First indeed torn with scourges over the whole body, then given to divers kinds of beasts, but guarded from these by divine power, after the added ferocity of fire and of iron, they completed their martyrdom. This glorious multitude Tyrannio and Silvanus urged on to victory, and also Peleus and Linus, bishops, Zenobius too, presbyter, who by a happy contest obtained, together with them, the palm of martyrdom. In the island of Cyprus, of the saints Potamius, and Nemesius. At Alemannia, of Saint Gall, presbyter and confessor.

## The ninth day before the Kalends · 21 February

[0781]

At Sicily, of the holy martyrs seventy-nine, who under Diocletian, through divers torments, deserved to receive the crown of their confession prepared for them by Christ. In Africa, in the city of Adrumetum, of the saints Verolus, secundinus, Servulus and twenty others. [Bouillart, at the edge of the page: At the monastery of Saint Germanus, the consecration of the altar in honour of the blessed martyrs John and Paul and of Saint Blasius, and also of the holy confessors Benedict, Lupus and Egidius. Also the consecration of the altar in honour of the Holy Innocents and of the holy virgins Columba, Margaret, Catherine.]

## The eighth day before the Kalends · 22 February

[0785]

At Antioch, of the Chair [Bouillart: *Cathedra*] of Saint Peter. On the same day, of blessed Papias, bishop of the city of Hierapolis, who was a hearer of John the apostle, but a fellow disciple and companion of Polycarpus. Also, of Saint Aristion, who was one of the seventy-two disciples of Christ. At Alexandria, of Saint Abilius, bishop, who, second bishop after blessed Mark, conspicuous in virtue, ministered the priesthood thirteen years, [In Bouillart, at the edge of the page: On the same day the consecration of the altar in honour of the blessed martyrs Eustachius and his companions, and of Saint Medard, confessor of Christ.]

## The seventh day before the Kalends · 23 February

[0787]

At Syrmium, of blessed Sinerus, monk and martyr, who, seized at the command of the emperor Maximian, when he confessed that he was a Christian, was beheaded. Also the birthday of sixty-two, who, completing the contest of martyrdom in the aforesaid city, received the abiding kingdoms. On this same day, of Saint Policarpus, presbyter and confessor, who with blessed Sebastian converted very many to the faith of Christ, and by exhorting led them to the glory of martyrdom.

## The sixth day before the Kalends · 24 February

[0791]

The birthday of blessed Matthias the apostle, who after the ascension of the Lord, chosen by lot by the apostles, at Judaea the Gospel of Christ, preached. Also, the finding of the head of the Forerunner of the Lord, in the time of the emperor Marcian, when the same Forerunner first revealed to two monks where that same head of his lay hidden. In Caesarea of Cappadocia, of Saint Sergius, martyr, whose most illustrious acts are extant.

## The fifth day before the Kalends · 25 February

[0793]

At Egypt, the birthday of the saints Victorinus, Victor, Nicoforus, Claudianus, Dioscorus, Serapion and Papias under the emperor Numerian: of whom the first, second and third steadfastly enduring exquisite kinds of punishments for the confession of the Godhead, the remaining four, Claudianus and Dioscorus, burned with flames. Serapion [sic: *Serapionis*] and Papias were slain with the sword. All of them therefore dedicated a celebrated martyrdom.

## The fourth day before the Kalends · 26 February

[0797]

In the city of Perge of Pamphylia, the birthday of blessed Nestor, bishop, who in the persecution of Decius, when he was intent upon prayer day and night, asking that the flock of Christ might be guarded, was seized, and, having confessed the name of the Lord with wonderful freedom and eagerness, was most cruelly tortured on the rack. Thence by hanging on the cross he passed away a victor. At Alexandria, of Saint Alexander, bishop, a glorious old man. He, after blessed Peter, cast out of the church Arius, his presbyter, depraved by heretical impiety and convicted by divine truth, and afterwards, among the three hundred and eighteen Fathers, condemned the same also in the council of Nicaea.

## The third day before the Kalends · 27 February

[0799]

At Alexandria, the passion of Saint Julian, martyr. He, since he was so bound by gout that he could neither walk nor stand, together with Eunus his servant, is presented to the judge in a chair; who, set upon camels, are ordered to be led about through the whole city, and to be torn with scourges on this side and that, the people looking on, until they met their end in the very beatings. In the Spains, in the city of Seville, the birthday of Saint Leander, bishop and confessor, by whose preaching and industry the whole nation of the Goths was converted from the Arian impiety through King Recharedus. At Lyon, of Saint Baldomeris, a man of God, whose tomb is made illustrious by frequent miracles.

## The day before the Kalends · 28 February

[0803]

In the territory of Lyon, in the Jura places, the deposition of blessed Romanus, abbot, who first led the hermit's life there, and, renowned for many virtues and miracles, afterwards became the father of very many monks. On the same day, of the saints Macharius and Rufinus.

## MARCH HAS 31 DAYS.

[0805]

## On the Kalends · 1 March

[0805]

At Rome, of the holy martyrs two hundred and sixty, whom Claudius first ordered, condemned for the name of Christ, to dig sand. Then he commanded that they be sent outside the walls of the Salarian gate, and be killed in the amphitheatre of the same city by the arrows of soldiers. On the same day, of Saint Donatus, martyr, who suffered at Carthage under the duke Ursacius and Marcellinus the tribune. At Angers, of Saint Albanus [Bouillart: *Albini*], bishop and confessor, a man of most illustrious virtue and holiness. In the city of Marseille, of the saints Hermes and Adrianus.

## The sixth day before the Nones · 2 March

[0809]

At Rome on the Latin Way, of the holy martyrs Jovinus and Basileus, who suffered under the emperors Gallienus and Valerian. Also at Rome, of very many martyrs, whom, long tortured, the emperor Alexander at the last condemned by capital sentence.



## The fifth day before the Nones · 3 March

[0811]

At Caesarea of Palestine, of the holy martyrs Marinus, soldier, and Asterius, senator, under the persecution of Valerian; of whom the former, when he had been accused by his fellow soldiers of being a Christian, and he testified with a most clear voice that he was a Christian, received the crown of martyrdom by the cutting off of his head. And when the latter received upon his shoulders set beneath it, and upon the garment he was wearing spread under it, the martyr's beheaded body, the honour which he paid to the martyr he himself at once received as a martyr. On the same day, the birthday of the saints Emetherius and Celedonius, who, at first soldiers at the city *Legionensis* of Gallicia, when the storm of persecution arose, afflicted with very many torments for the confession of the name of Christ, were led as far as Calagurris, and there were crowned with martyrdom.

## The fourth day before the Nones · 4 March

[0815]

At Rome on the Appian Way, the birthday of blessed Lucius, pope and martyr, who, in the persecution of Valerian and Gallienus, banished into exile for the faith of Christ, and afterwards by the divine will permitted to return to his church, completed his martyrdom by the cutting off of his head. Also at Rome on the Appian Way, of the holy martyrs nine hundred, who are laid in the cemetery at Saint Cecilia. On the same day, of Saint Caius, of the palace, drowned in the sea.

## The third day before the Nones · 5 March

[0817]

At Antioch, the birthday of blessed Focas, martyr, who, after the many injuries which he suffered for the name of the Redeemer, how he triumphed over that ancient serpent is declared to the peoples even today. On this same day, the passion of Saint Eusebius, of the palace, and of nine other martyrs.

## The day before the Nones · 6 March

[0819]

At Nicomedia, the birthday of the saints Victor and Victorinus, who for three years, with Claudianus and Bassa his wife, afflicted with many torments and thrust back into prison, there fulfilled the course of their life. In the city of Toledo, the deposition of Julian, bishop, who is held most famous among the inhabitants of the same place.

## On the Nones · 7 March

[0821]

In Mauritania, in the city of the Tuburbitani, the birthday of the holy martyrs Perpetua and Felicitas, and with them of Revocatus, Saturninus and Secundolus, of whom the last rested in prison, all the rest were given to the beasts under the emperor Severus.

## The eighth day before the Ides · 8 March

[0825]

In the city of Antinoum, the birthday of the saints Philemon and Apollonius, deacon, who, seized and heard by the judge, when they had steadfastly refused to sacrifice to idols, their heels pierced, were dragged horribly through the city, and at the last, slain with the sword, completed their martyrdom. On the same day at the aforesaid city, the passion of Arrianus, Theoticus, and three others; whom the judge killed, sunk in the sea, but by the service of a dolphin their bodies were restored to the shore. At Carthage, of Saint Pontius, deacon of blessed Cyprian, bishop, who, bearing exile with him up to the day of his passion, left an excellent volume of his life and passion, and, renowned in sufferings, merited the crown of life.

## The seventh day before the Ides · 9 March

[0827]

At the city of Nisena the deposition of Saint Gregory, bishop, brother of blessed Basil of Caesarea as most illustrious in life as in eloquence. In the city of Barcelona, of Saint Patianus, bishop who, in the time of the emperor Theodosius, in an excellent old age obtained the end of his life.

## The sixth day before the Ides · 10 March

[0829]

At Apamia, the birthday of the saints Alexander and Gaius, martyrs, who, as Apollinaris, bishop of Hierapolis, writes in the book *Against the Catafrigae*, in the persecution of Antoninus Verus were crowned with a glorious martyrdom In Persis, of the holy martyrs to the number of forty-two. At Paris, the deposition of Saint Droctoveus, abbot disciple of blessed Germanus, bishop. [Bouillart adds: On this same day, [nt: Here Sollerius summons the Pratensis codex to court, because Saint Attalus is added to the saints of this day; since not a few handwritten codices, and those of any worth you please, do not commemorate that holy abbot, and others do so in another manner: it is not credible, he says, that he would have been absent from those manuscripts if the source itself, from which those streamlets were drawn, had had him: he therefore suspects that the words of the Pratensis are more recent. That he may refute his own petty reasonings himself, I ask one thing: that he come and inspect the codex. For what weight have conjectures against what really is? Nor let him object the erasure to us. For he confesses that both the forty-two martyrs and Droctoveus the abbot are Usuardus's, and yet they too are written on the same erasure as Attalus. Nor yet do I deny that Attalus was added, since the Dervensis codex is silent about him. But Usuardus was free to enrich his Martyrology when he pleased, and with what saints he pleased. Nor was it necessary that he should send his codex anywhere at all the moment he had corrected something in it, or make known by letter what he had added to the codex and what he had taken away. That this is the day on which Saint Attalus, or Attala, ought to have been commemorated, there is no need for me to prove. His Acts are in everyone's hands. Bouillart.] of Saint Attalus, abbot, disciple of Saint Columbanus.]

## The fifth day before the Ides · 11 March

[0833]

At Sebaste of Lesser Armenia, the birthday of the forty holy soldiers, who, in the time of King Licinius, after chains and very frequent imprisonments, after their faces were beaten with stones, were sent into a pool, and so at length completed their martyrdom by the breaking of their legs. And the more noble [nt: The Pratensis codex omitted the word 'nobiliores'. The observation is Sollerius's. Yet there is no word in the whole article that strikes the eyes more forcibly. Bouillart.] among them were Quirion and Candidus.

## The fourth day before the Ides · 12 March

[0835]

At Rome, of the blessed pontiffs Gregory, doctor, and apostle of the English, and Innocent. At Nicomedia, the passion of Saint Peter, martyr. He, since he was chamberlain of the emperor Diocletian, and complained too freely of the immense punishments of the martyrs, at the command of the same is brought out into the midst, and first, hung up, he is tortured very long with scourges, then, drenched with vinegar and salt, at the last he is roasted on a gridiron, and so he stood forth heir both of the faith and of the name of the true Peter. Also at Nicomedia, of the saints Egdunus, presbyter, and seven others, who were suffocated day by day, that fear might be struck into the rest.

## The third day before the Ides · 13 March

[0839]

[0839]At Nicomedia, the birthday of the holy martyrs Macedonius, presbyter, Patricia and Modesta. In the city of Nicaea, of the holy martyrs Theuseta, Horris, Theodora, Nimpodora, Mark, Arabia, who were all given over to the fire. In the Thebaid, the deposition of Saint Eufrasia, virgin.

## The day before the Ides · 14 March

[0841]

At Rome, the passion of the saints forty-seven. These were baptized by blessed Peter the apostle, when he was held in the custody of the Mamertine, with his fellow apostle Paul, where they were detained nine months; all of whom, under a most devoted confession of the faith, were consumed by the Neronian sword. In Africa, of Saint Peter, martyr. Also of Saint Eufrosius.

## On the Ides · 15 March

[0843]

In Caesarea of Cappadocia, the passion of Saint Longinus, who pierced the side of the Lord with a lance, as is found in his acts. At the city of Thessalonica, the birthday of Saint Matrona, martyr, who, caught and afflicted in many ways, at the last beaten to death with stout cudgels, in the confession of Christ rendered her spirit uncorrupted to God.

## The seventeenth day before the Kalends · 16 March

[0847]

At [nt: In the Caroline autograph mention of Saints Hilary and Tatianus was never made. For the Dervensis codex is silent about them, and takes the beginning of the article from Cyriacus. Besides, in the Pratensis this whole article suffers from an erasure from head to foot, and, so that there might be room for those saints, it is written out entire in a smaller form of letters. Nor again do the Heriniensis and Tornacensis codices commemorate those saints, which were for the most part Sollerius's standard by which to value the Pratensis. Here I ask Sollerius for what cause he preferred the Pratensis and departed from his own. In the Pratensis there was an erasure, the other codices varied. On these two arguments alone he everywhere judged the Pratensis codex interpolated. In this place, therefore, or nowhere, his rule ought to have had room Yet Sollerius gives the whole article: it is wholly Usuardus's, pure Usuardus. Of the erasure not even a word from the censor; I suppose, because he was advised that there is no dissimilarity of script there, and that it is to be counted to Usuardus's praise that, after the example of eminent writers, he neither thought an erasure in his writings shameful nor feared it. Why in the same case Sollerius was not always of the same mind toward the Pratensis codex, I would rather not know than suspect anything maliciously of the zeal for truth with which he declares that he burns. Bouillart.] Aquileia, the birthday of blessed Hilary, bishop, and Tatianus, deacon, who under the governor Beronius, after the rack and other torments, together with Felix, Largus, and Dionysius, ended their martyrdom. At Rome, the passion of Saint Cyriacus, deacon, who after a long wasting in prison, drenched with melted pitch and stretched upon the scaffold, and dragged, beaten also with thongs and cudgels, at the last, with Largus and Smaragdus and twenty others, at the command of Maximinus, was beheaded. Their feast, however, is kept on the sixth day before the Ides of August, on which day their bodies were raised by blessed Marcellus, pope, and reverently entombed. At Arverni, the deposition of Saint Patrick, bishop and confessor.

## The sixteenth day before the Kalends · 17 March

[0849]

In Scotia, the birthday of Saint Patrick, bishop and confessor, who first preached Christ there. [0851] On the same day, at the monastery of Nivigella, of Saint Gertrude, virgin. [In Bouillart . . . . : preached. In the city of Nicomedia, of the holy martyrs Eugenius, Pamphilianus, Castor and Serenus [nt: Sollerius hesitates whether to call the codex corrupted or altered. Four holy martyrs both badly joined and wrongly brought over here. Gertrude thrust out of her place and ineptly inserted among the saints of the following day, two texts corrupted by one error. And these injuries he pours out over the erasure of a single line, he who a little before bore the erasure of nine whole lines with a quiet and even mind. What do I say to this? It is true that those holy martyrs were not commemorated in the Caroline autograph; but that they were either badly joined or wrongly drawn here, by what argument will Sollerius make out? Has he any Acts to bring forward? He will thrust the Hieronymian lists upon us, I know well enough: but in their most ancient codices not even one of those is read of whom Usuardus speaks here. Nor had it been dealt with on the day before. For so they have it, on the witness of Henschenius: At Nicomedia, of Castor, Dionysius, Nonnus, Cyriaca, Milisa, Eugenia, Julian, Asclepiodotus. Other codices indeed announce Castor, others Serenus, others, one class having been made out of two, Pamphilianus. What certainty can be beaten out of that conflict of codices? Perhaps Usuardus had other lists; perhaps he joined both classes of the Nicomedian martyrs on one day; perhaps he saw Acts. In short, I would rather conjecture anything at all than, like Sollerius, reject with no argument a codex not at all suspect. Of Saint Gertrude presently, in the following article. Bouillart.].]

## The fifteenth day before the Kalends · 18 March

[0853]

The birthday of blessed Alexander, bishop, who, coming from Cappadocia, from his own city, to Jerusalem with a holy desire, by divine revelation thereupon took up the government of that place, and, after a venerable old age, led to Caesarea, in the persecution of Decius completed his martyrdom for the confession of Christ. [Bouillart adds: [nt: This is the true place of Saint Gertrude. And I wonder how Henschenius and others could be deceived, who recorded the death of that holy Virgin on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of this month. Usuardus himself had gone astray in the Caroline autograph; but he fittingly corrected the error in his own: the same Acts which had deceived him, weighed more diligently, brought him back into the way. The writer of the Life relates that Blessed Gertrude, when the day of her death was at hand, sent one of the brothers to the monastery of Fosses, to ask of Ultan, a holy dweller of that place, on what day she was to die: that Ultan answered: Today is the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April. But tomorrow, during the solemnities of the Mass, that handmaid of God and virgin of Christ is to depart from the body: that Gertrude, on receiving this message, spent the whole night with the sisters in psalms and prayers, and on the morrow, a Sunday, gave up her spirit. That Sunday, therefore, was the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April. Gertrude therefore did not die in the year 664, as Henschenius thinks; nor in the year 659, as the most distinguished (v. cl.) Baillet prefers: but in the year 658, in which Easter fell on 25 March, lunar cycle 13, solar 23, Dominical Letter G. Why, you will say, do the same Acts report that she died on a Sunday, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April? The Acts, badly copied, do indeed report it; but that the reading must be kept which our Mabillon drew from the Feuillant codex is plain even from this, that otherwise the writer of the Life would not be consistent with himself. For if Gertrude was to die on the day after XVI Kal. Apr., how could she die on XVI Kal. April? Bouillart.] At the monastery of Nivigella, of Saint Geretrudis, virgin.]

## The fourteenth day before the Kalends · 19 March

[0855D]

The birthday of blessed John, a man of great holiness, who, a native of Syria, came to Italy: and there, having built a monastery at the city *Penarensis*, being for forty years the father of many servants of God, renowned for many virtues he rested in peace. On the same day at Surrentum, of the saints Quintus, Quintillus, Quartilla, Mark, with nine others. In the city of Brixa, of Saint Calocerus [nt: Not only the name of Calocerus, as Castellanus noted, but also that whole space from *sanctorum* to the end has been deleted. Nor yet does this prevent the text of the Usuardine codex from seeming pure to Sollerius. And certainly not wrongly, since the hand is the same. But it is worth knowing for what reason he pays such honour to the Pratensis codex: namely, because all the codices of best credit with one accord placed Calocerus on this day. The order of argument will perhaps seem preposterous, especially since with Sollerius the Pratensis codex holds the first place by title of antiquity. Bouillart.], martyr.

## The thirteenth day before the Kalends · 20 March

[0859]

In Asia, the birthday of Saint Archippus, fellow soldier of blessed Paul, of whom the same Apostle makes mention in his epistle, writing to the Colossians. At Britain, the deposition of Saint Cuthbert, who from an anchorite became bishop of the church of Lindisfarne, and led his whole life, from infancy to old age, renowned for the signs of miracles. In Syria, of the saints Paul, Cyril, Eugenius with four others. On this same day, of Saint Vulfrannus, confessor.

## The twelfth day before the Kalends · 21 March

[0861]

At the fortress of Cassinum, the birthday of Saint Benedict, abbot, the life of this man, glorious in virtues and miracles, blessed Pope Gregory writes. At Alexandria, of blessed Serapion, anchorite, a man of great virtues. In the territory of Lyon, of Saint Lupicinus, abbot, whose life was illustrious for holiness, and for the glory of miracles.

## The eleventh day before the Kalends · 22 March

[0863]

At Septimania, in the city of Biterris, the deposition of Saint Afrodisius, bishop and confessor. He, ordained bishop for the same city by blessed Paul, [0865] bishop of Narbonne, distinguished in the teachings of the faith and adorned with the merits of virtues, rested in peace.

## The tenth day before the Kalends · 23 March

[0867]

In Africa, of the holy martyrs Victorianus, Frumentius, and another Frumentius, and two brothers, who, in the Vandal persecution, as Victor, an African bishop, writes, under King Huneric, for the constancy of their catholic confession, tortured with most savage punishments, were crowned with an excellent martyrdom. At Antioch, of Saint Theodorus, presbyter. In the city of Caesarea, of Saint Julian.

## The ninth day before the Kalends · 24 March

[0869]

At Rome, the passion of blessed Pigmenius, presbyter. He nourished Julian the apostate from a boy and instructed him in sacred letters, by whom he himself was afterwards put to death in the Tiber for the faith of Christ. In Mauritania, the birthday of the saints Romulus and Secundolus, brothers, who were born for Christ. At Syria, of Saint Seleucus. Also in Phrygia, of Saint Agapitus.

## The eighth day before the Kalends · 25 March

[0871]

At Nazareth, a city of Galilee, the Annunciation of the Lord. At Sirmium, the passion of blessed Hireneus, bishop, in the time of the emperor Maximian, who, first vexed with most bitter torments, then tortured in prison for very many days, at the last was consummated by the cutting off of his head. At Rome, of Saint Cyrinus, martyr. who, after the loss of his property, after the filth of prison, after the affliction of many blows, was slain with the sword by King Claudius. At Nicomedia, the birthday of Dula, the handmaid of a certain soldier, who was slain for her chastity. In the island of Antrum of Saint Hermelandus, abbot, whose glorious manner of life is praised by the proclamation of miracles.



## The seventh day before the Kalends · 26 March

[0875]

At Pentapolis of Libya, the birthday of the saints Theodorus, bishop, Hireneus, deacon, Serapion and Ammonius, readers. At Rome on the Lavican Way, of Saint Castolus, martyr, who, as is read in the acts of blessed Sebastian, hung up by the persecutors three times, heard three times, persevering in the confession of the Lord, was sent into a pit, and, a mass of sand being let down upon him, passed to Christ by martyrdom. At Sirmium, of the saints Montanus, presbyter, and Maxima, drowned in the sea.

## The sixth day before the Kalends · 27 March

[0879]

In Egypt, the deposition of blessed John, hermit, who, among the other marks of virtues, full also of the prophetic spirit, foretold to the most Christian emperor Theodosius his victories over the tyrant. In Pannonia, of Saint Alexander, martyr. [Bouillart adds: [nt: That Saint Eucherius ought to have been placed by Usuardus on this day, Castellanus and Sollerius not wrongly deny. But that he was placed there, no one but an obstinate man, or one plainly a stranger in judging scripts, will deny. If Usuardus sinned, it is at his own peril. Bouillart.] On this same day, of Saint Eucherius, bishop of Tours.]

## The fifth day before the Kalends · 28 March

[0881]

In Caesarea of Palestine, of the holy martyrs Priscus, Malchus, Alexander, who in the persecution of Valerian, kindled by the divine heat of faith, going of their own accord to the judge, rebuke him for his savagery against the blood of the godly; whom he at once gave to the beasts to be devoured for the name of Christ. At the city of the Cabilonenses, the deposition of Saint Guntramnus, king, who so gave himself over to spiritual works that, leaving behind the pomps of the world, he paid out his treasures to churches and to the poor. At Tarsus of Cilicia, of Castor and Dorotheus.

## The fourth day before the Kalends · 29 March

[0883]

At Africa, the birthday of the holy confessors Armogastus, Archinimus and Satyrus, who, in the time of the Vandal persecution, under King Geisericus, having endured many and grievous punishments and reproaches for the confession of the truth, [0885] fulfilled the course of a glorious contest. On this same day, the deposition of Eustasius, abbot of the monastery *Luxoviensis*, who was the Father of almost six hundred monks, and, conspicuous for holiness of life, shone also with miracles. [Bouillart, after the African martyrs: [nt: This last commemoration of the saints Pastor and Victorinus is written on an erasure in the same hand as the rest of the article: after it a space of two lines and a half is left empty of all writing, nay, so scraped with the knife that not even the eyes of a lynx could detect a trace of any little letter. Other codices lack Pastor and Victorinus, and after the African confessors set a long commemoration (*commemoratiouem*, printed so) of Saint Eustasius. Hence Sollerius's complaints, that Pastor and Victorinus were added, Saint Eustasius expelled, and the codex therefore depraved. Had he said altered, I should find nothing to blame; for I freely confess that the Nicomedian (*Nicomendienses*, printed so) martyrs were absent from the Caroline autograph and that Saint Eustasius was present. But how would Sollerius prove that the codex was therefore depraved? Is it because, as he says, Pastor and Victorinus have been torn away from a larger band? But of the codices which he cites in great number there are scarcely two that agree with one another about that band, so that to Sollerius himself the number seems to be changed at will. Doubtless the other codices could with impunity increase and diminish the band at will; the Pratensis alone is at fault (*vftio*, printed so). I pass over what he adds, that those two martyrs are passed over by the other codices. For first, that is false; for the Rosweydinus and the Aquicinctinus, which Sollerius judges to be of the best mark, record them among others. The Gellone martyrology, too, made public by our d'Achery, records them. I do not add the exemplars of the Prés: that would be number, not authority. They are had, moreover, by the Matricula Carthus.-Ultraject. and the Galesinian edition. Next, even if they were lacking in all the codices, nothing would follow from that against the Pratensis. It is a correction of which the other Churches either were not advised, or which, being advised, they neglected. I do not doubt that Usuardus reserved Saint Eustasius for the second day of April for just causes, although Ado of Vienne placed him on this day. Without doubt he saw Acts which have now perished. Perhaps too he was led to it by the Hieronymian lists, whose most ancient codex, which I have before my eyes, is silent about Eustasius today and commemorates him on the second of April. Bouillart.] In the city of Nicomedia, the passion of the saints Pastor and Victorinus.]

## The third day before the Kalends · 30 March

[0887]

At Rome on the Appian Way, the passion of blessed Quirinus, tribune and martyr, who under the emperor Aurelian, after the cutting out of his tongue and hanging on the rack, and the cutting off of his hands and feet, consummated the contest of martyrdom by the sword. At Thessalonica, the birthday of the saints Domninus, and Victor. [Bouillart: [nt: Most codices add to Domninus as companion Victor, who was never a companion of Domninus. But by I know not what fate it happened that Usuardus, not knowing them at first, put I know not whom there; but afterwards, instructed by new information, he excluded him and gave room to the two others. And this is enough for Sollerius to strike the Pratensis codex off the roll of the pure, to affirm that Usuardus's sense has vanished, and to ascribe the correction to some smatterer. In vain will you show him the same hand: his codices give Victor. Filopolus and Achaicus, therefore, are not Usuardus's. And so the Pratensis codex must lose the title of autograph, because Usuardus, as soon as he had emended anything, did not take care to have it posted at all the crossroads of all cities, so that what he himself had corrected others too might correct. Nor is this the only fault in this article that Sollerius reproaches. He is also indignant that Saint Regulus, bishop of Senlis, was erased. [0891]

Of Amos the prophet, whom Ozias, king of Israel, killed, pierced through the temples with a bar, and afterwards, half alive, he was carried to his homeland and there was buried. At Rome, of Saint Balbina, virgin, daughter of Quirinus the martyr, who, after the course of this world was overcome, is buried on the Appian Way beside her father. In Africa, of the saints Diodolus and Anesius.

## APRIL HAS 30 DAYS.

[0893]

## On the Kalends · 1 April

[0893]

At Rome, the passion of most blessed Theodora, sister of the most illustrious martyr Hermes. She, martyred under the emperor Aurelian, was buried beside her brother on the Salarian Way, not far from the city of Rome. On the same day, of Saint venantius, bishop and martyr. In Egypt, of the saints Victor and Stephen.

## The fourth day before the Nones · 2 April

[0897]

At Caesarea of Cappadocia, the passion of Saint Theodosia, virgin, who, in the time of Diocletian, joining herself of her own accord to the confessors in custody, was seized and nonetheless tortured on the rack, by the power of God afterwards rescued from chains, waters, beasts, at the last completed her martyrdom by the cutting off of her head. On the same day, the birthday of blessed Nicetius, bishop of Lyon, whose life shone with miracles, and whose precious death is nonetheless commended by miracles. At Palestine, [nt: Sirmond had once read Mary the Egyptian in the third place, and in the fourth Saint Eustasius. For how can these things be reconciled? If Sirmond read Mary the Egyptian, how was she struck out? If she was struck out, how did Sirmond read her? For my part, had I been in Sollerius's place, this alone would have brought it about that I should put no faith in Castellanus's eyes. Now I teach Sollerius how the codex stands in this place. [0901]

At Thessalonica, the passion of the holy virgins Agapes and Chionia under Diocletian, who, first wasted in prison, afterwards sent into the fire, but untouched by the flames, after prayer poured out to the Lord, gave up their souls. At Tauromenium of Sicily, of blessed Pancratius.

## The day before the Nones · 4 April

[0903]

At Milan, the deposition of blessed Ambrose, bishop and confessor, by whose zeal, among the other marks of doctrine and of miracles, in the time of the Arian perfidy, the whole of Italy was converted to the catholic faith. At Seville, the deposition of Saint Isidore, prelate.

## On the Nones · 5 April

[0905]

At Egypt, the birthday of the holy martyrs Martiana, Nicanor, and Apollonius. At Thessalonica, of Saint Hirene, virgin, who, after enduring prison, was struck with an arrow by Sisinnius the count, under whom her sisters also, Agapes and Chionia, were martyred together. At Caesarea of Licia, of Saint Amphianus.

## The eighth day before the Ides · 6 April

[0909]

At Rome, the birthday of blessed Sixtus, pope and martyr, who in the times of Hadrian, that he might gain Christ for himself, willingly endured temporal death. In Macedonia, of the saints Timotheus and Diogenes.

## The seventh day before the Ides · 7 April

[0911]

At Africa, the birthday of the saints Epiphanius, bishop, Donatus and thirteen others. On the same day, of Egesippus, a most holy man, who, near to the times of the Apostles, wove together all the histories of ecclesiastical deeds from the passion of the Lord up to his own age, so that he might express also the manner of speaking of those whose life he followed. At Alexandria, of Saint Pelusius, presbyter.

## The sixth day before the Ides · 8 April

[0915]

At Corinth, of blessed Dionisius, bishop, by whose learning and grace, which he had in the word of God, many profit even to this day. And this chosen one of Christ likewise shone in the times of Marcus Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius. At Tours, of Saint Perpetuus, bishop, a man of admirable holiness.

## The fifth day before the Ides · 9 April

[0917]

The birthday of blessed Procorus, who was one of the first seven deacons; he, renowned in faith and miracles, was consummated by martyrdom at Antioch. At Sirmium, the passion of the seven holy virgins, who, paying together the price of their blood, purchased eternal life.

## The fourth day before the Ides · 10 April

[0919]

Of Ezekiel the prophet, who, slain by the judge of the people of Israel at Babylonia, was buried in the tomb of Sem and Arfaxad. At Rome, of very many blessed martyrs, whom Saint Alexander, pope, baptized when he was held in prison. All these the emperor Aurelian caused to be put on board an old ship, to be led out into the deep sea, and there, stones being tied to their necks, to be sunk in the depth of the sea. At Alexandria, of Saint Appolonius, presbyter, and five others.

## The third day before the Ides · 11 April

[0921]

At Rome, the birthday of blessed Leo, pope, in whose times there was the holy synod of Chalcedon. At Crete, in the city of Gortina, of Saint Philip, bishop, who was endowed with great virtues and the best studies. And he flourished [0923] in the times of the emperors Antoninus Verus and Lucius Aurelius. In Dalmatia, in the city of Salona, of Saint Domio, bishop, with eight soldiers. At Nicomedia, of Saint Eustorgius, presbyter.

## The day before the Ides · 12 April

[0925]

At Rome on the Aurelian Way, the birthday of blessed Julius, pope, who, having endured tribulations and exiles for ten months under the emperor Constantius, after his death returned with great glory to his see, and rested in peace. [Bouillart inserts: On the same day, [nt: The mention of Zeno, although made on another leaf, shows the same form of letters, the same ink, the same parchment, so that only a blind man, or a most unskilled judge of scripts, could blurt out that it was intruded after Usuardus. No erasure, a clean character, nothing that could cast suspicion into even captious judges. Almost all the codices known to Sollerius support it. Of those I have gone through, none dissents: four of the Prés of the best mark, two of which exceed five hundred years, two Victorine, the Conchensis, that of Pontoise, the Feuillant A, B, the Colbertine A, B, C, D, that of Fossés: the books more correctly and accurately edited agree, as Sollerius admits: an ancient martyrology written at the beginning of the eleventh century and carefully kept at Paris in the royal priory of Saint-Martin gives the same reading: the Roman Martyrology commemorates the same Zeno on the same day. And shall a reading propped by so many supports totter and be imperilled? Without doubt Sollerius saw codices to set against the Pratensis. So it is: he saw two, the Heriniensis and the Tornacensis; let him add the Dervensis too, it is nothing to me. It was no concern of the other Churches that whatever had been emended by Usuardus they too should emend. But, destitute of codices, he fights perhaps with arguments, and those indeed such as cannot be answered. He must be heard. Very rarely, he says, does Usuardus summon Transalpine saints. What then, pray? If very rarely, then sometimes. And Zeno will be one of those. But Usuardus's narrative is more than doubtful. Why then did Henschenius hesitate in doubt whether to assert Zeno pontiff and confessor only, or martyr as well? Has Sollerius found out anything new? But Henschenius pronounces expressly, with no argument indeed, but yet expressly pronounces, that Zeno was intruded by later men. I would not dare to answer. And what will the reader think of this urbanity of Sollerius? I would dare to suspect that there was someone, a fellow initiate (symmistes) of Usuardus... who thought his own style must be tempered to Usuardus's. Bouillart.] of Saint Zeno, bishop, who amid the storms of persecution wonderfully ruled the city of Verona, and in the time of Gallienus was crowned with martyrdom.] At Vapingum, the deposition of Constantinus, bishop.

## On the Ides · 13 April

[0929]

At Pergamum, a city of Asia, the birthday of the saints Carpus, bishop. Papirius, deacon, and Agathonica, an excellent woman, and of many other women, who for their blessed confessions were crowned with martyrdom under Antoninus Verus and Aurelius Commodus. [Bouillart, at the edge of the page: On the same day at the monastery of Saint Germanus, the consecration of the altar in honour of the holy and undivided Trinity and of the life-giving cross, and also of the most blessed Mother of God, Mary, and of Saint Guandregisilus, and also of all the saints.]

## The eighteenth day before the Kalends · 14 April

[0933]

At Rome on the Appian Way, the birthday of the most blessed martyrs Tiburtius, Valerian and Maximus, Almachius being prefect, of whom the first were beaten with cudgels, struck with the sword, the last was beaten with leaded scourges so long, until he breathed out his spirit. At Alexandria, of Saint Fronto, abbot, whose life stood forth glorious in holiness and miracles. At Interamna, of blessed Proculus, martyr. Also, of Saint Domnina, virgin, crowned with her companion virgins.

## The seventeenth day before the Kalends · 15 April

[0935]

At Persis, in the city of Cordula, the birthday of the saints Olympias, and Maximus, nobles, who at the command of Decius were beaten with cudgels, and then with leaded scourges, at the last their heads were beaten with axes, until they gave up their spirit. In Italy, of the blessed martyrs Maro, Euticetis and Victorinus, who, first leading a long exile at the island Pontia in the confession of Christ, afterwards under the emperor Nerva, when they had converted very many to the faith, were ordered to be slain by various punishments.

## The sixteenth day before the Kalends · 16 April

[0937]

At Corinth, the birthday of the saints Callistus and Carisius, with seven others, all drowned in the sea. At Caesaraugusta, of the eighteen holy martyrs Quintilianus, Cassianus, Matutinus, Publius, Urbanus, Martialis, [0939] Faustus, Successus, Felix, Januarius, Primitivus, Evotus, Cecilianus, Optatus, Fronto, Lupercus, Apodemus, and Julius. These all together, under Datianus, governor of the Spains, were afflicted with punishments and slain.

## The fifteenth day before the Kalends · 17 April

[0941]

At Africa, the birthday of Saint Mappalicus, martyr, who, as blessed Cyprian writes in the epistle to the martyrs and confessors, was crowned with many others. At Antioch, of the holy martyrs Peter, deacon, and Hermogenes. [Bouillart inserts: [nt: In the Pratensis codex, between the Antiochene and the Cordoban martyrs, mention is made of Nicephorus. Yet the Pratensis was not worthy for Sollerius to follow, both on account of other codices which lack Nicephorus, and most of all because, as Castellanus advised, what is said of Nicephorus was wholly intruded, and that by a hand not very ancient. Am I to hear so often of the same thing? Am I so often to deafen the reader about the same thing? But here I wish Sollerius to learn more about our codex from me than he learned from Castellanus. The last line of the page, where Peter the deacon and Hermogenes are now seen, was once almost wholly erased, and restored in another hand, though one nearest to the age of Usuardus, and in another ink. Let Sollerius turn over his notes again. Perhaps his informant said of those martyrs what he himself understands of Nicephorus. Next, the first two lines of the following page, where Nicephorus and the Cordoban monks are now read, were likewise erased. But let me have credit with Sollerius that the hand which wrote those saints is the very same as that of the rest of the codex; in a smaller form of letters, however, so that room might be given to Nicephorus, whom Usuardus brought in here, deceived beyond doubt by certain Acts which falsely claimed that the feast of Nicephorus was kept on this day. ## The fourteenth day before the Kalends · 18 April

[0945]

At Messana, a city of Apulia, the birthday of the holy martyrs Eleutherius, bishop, and Anthia his mother, who, since he was illustrious both for holiness of life and for the power of miracles, under the emperor Hadrian, overcoming a fiery iron bed, a gridiron and a frying pan boiling with oil, pitch, and resin, thrown also to lions, but unharmed by them, at the last has his throat cut together with his mother. At Rome, of blessed Apollonius, senator, who under the emperor Commodus, betrayed by a slave as being a Christian, composed a notable volume, which he read in the senate, and then by sentence of the senate was beheaded for Christ. At Cordoba, of Saint Perfectus, presbyter and martyr.

## The thirteenth day before the Kalends · 19 April

[0947]

[0947]Of blessed Thimo, deacon, of the first seven, who first settled as a teacher at Beroea, and then, sowing the word of the Lord, came to Corinth, and there by Jews and Greeks, as is handed down, was first cast into flames, but was harmed in nothing, then, fastened to a cross, fulfilled his martyrdom. In Armenia, in the city of Militana, the birthday of the holy martyrs Hermogenes, Gaius, expeditus, Aristonicus, Rufus, Galatae, crowned on one day. [0951]

In the Gauls, in the city of Ebredunum, of Saint Marcellus, bishop and confessor of the same city, who, by divine command, coming from Africa with his holy companions Vincent and Domninus, converted to the faith of Christ the greatest part [sic: *pratem*] of the Maritime Alps, by the word and by admirable signs, with which he shines even to this day. ## The eleventh day before the Kalends · 21 April

[0955]

At Persis, the birthday of blessed Simeon, bishop and martyr, who, at the command of Sapor, king of the Persians, seized and loaded with iron, when he testified of the Lord with a free and most constant voice, first wasted in a prison dungeon with a hundred others, of whom some were bishops, some presbyters, some clerics of divers orders, at the last was ordered to be beheaded together with them all. There suffered with him also certain most illustrious men, Ustazadis, Abdella, Ananias and Pusitius, with a daughter, who was a holy virgin. At Alexandria, of the saints Arator, presbyter, Fortunus, Felix, Silvius, Vitalis, who rested in prison.

## The tenth day before the Kalends · 22 April

[0957]

At Rome on the Appian Way, the birthday of blessed Gaius, pope, who, when he had ruled the Church eleven years, four months, twelve days, was crowned with martyrdom under the emperor Diocletian. At Persis, of the holy martyrs who had their throats cut with the sword for the name of Christ under King Sapor. In which contest of the faith there suffered Melisius, bishop, Acepsimas also, bishop, with James, presbyter. Mareas and Bicor, no less bishops, with clerics about two hundred and fifty, with monks also and very many consecrated virgins. Among whom also the sister of Simeon the bishop, Tarbua by name, with her maidservant, was cut through with a saw. In the city of Cordula, the birthday [0959] of Parmenius, Helimenae and Chrisotelus, presbyters, Luke and Mucius, deacons, the triumph of whose martyrdom is contained in the passion of blessed Lawrence. At Lyon, of Saint Epipodius, who, in the persecution of Antoninus Verus, after grievous torments inflicted upon him, completed his martyrdom by the cutting off of his head. The codices he surveyed (and he surveyed nearly eighty) were all so faulty that he dared trust none at all, and all had to be collated together so that he might draw the text out of each. The collation of each, he himself says, has given (*dubit*, printed so) the simplest text that could be. Let others praise the labour; I vehemently admire the acumen and judgment. For in such depravation of the codices, who would not wonder that Sollerius could so know Usuardus's sense that he did not depart from it even a nail's breadth, and rendered the autograph itself word for word? Certainly someone will suspect that, while he was working on this article, he had before his eyes the apograph which he keeps by him, and copied it out at least as far as 'Senones'. But that it is of the same hand as the rest of the article not even Sollerius denies. And on this very day the Church of Sens honours the memory of Saint Leo, the more ancient Martyrologies record it, Saussay's more recent one celebrates it with a eulogy. ## The ninth day before the Kalends · 23 April

[0963]

In Persis, in the city of Diospolis, the passion of Saint George, martyr, the acts of whose passion, although they are numbered among the apocryphal writings, yet the Church of God reverently honours his most illustrious martyrdom among the crowns of the martyrs. In the Gauls, in the city of Valentia, the birthday of the saints Felix, presbyter, Fortunatus and Achilleus, deacons, who, when they had converted the greatest part of the aforesaid city to the faith of Christ, were thrust into prison by the duke Cornelius, then beaten very long, and, their legs broken, bound about the whirling of wheels, having endured smoke also in their hanging on the rack, at the last were consummated by the sword. [Bouillart adds: [nt: In the Caroline autograph there was written: at the fortress of the Silvanectenses, the deposition of Saint Regulus, bishop and confessor. Here simply, bishop and confessor. Why did he omit 'deposition'? For there was space enough left for it to be added. Here I recognize the acumen and sagacity of Usuardus. He had certainly read the acts of Saint Regulus: but when he saw them full of fables, and that no faith could safely be placed in them, he consulted the Church which ought to have committed the deeds of Regulus and the day of his death to memory with the greater care. That Church, however, agrees so little with the Caroline autograph that it venerates the deposition on this day and the translation on 30 March. What was Usuardus to do? He deleted what he had written on XXX March. And lest, by marking the deposition which the Acts record today, he should be deceived, he held it enough to note the day sacred to Saint Regulus. ## The eighth day before the Kalends · 24 April

[0967]

At Lyon of Gaul, the birthday of Saint Alexander, martyr, who, in the persecution of Antoninus Verus, after the custody of prison, was first so torn by the cruelty of those beating him that, the framework of his ribs loosened, his bowels laid open, the inward parts of his body were exposed. ## The fifth day before the Kalends · 27 April

## The fourth day before the Kalends · 28 April

[0979]

## The third day before the Kalends · 29 April

At Paphos, of Saint Tychicus, deacon, disciple of blessed Paul. Of him the same Apostle makes mention in his epistles, declaring him to be his dearest brother and fellow servant in the Lord. In Numidia, at the colony *Cirtensis*, the birthday of the holy martyrs Agapius and Secundinus, bishops, who, in the persecution of Valerian, after a long exile, at the aforesaid city, in which the rage of the gentiles was then most eagerly gaping to try the faith of the just, from illustrious priesthood were made glorious martyrs. There suffered in their company Emilianus, a soldier, Tertulla and Antonia, holy virgins, and a certain woman with her twins.

## The day before the Kalends · 30 April

[0987]

At the city *Lambesitana*, the birthday of the holy martyrs Marianus, reader, and James, deacon, of whom the former, when he had long before overcome the assault of the Decian persecution in the confession of Christ, again seized with his dearest colleague. Then, after dire and exquisite punishments, wonderfully strengthened and relieved a second time by divine revelations, at the last they were consummated by the sword with many others. In the city of Sanctonas, of blessed Euprobus, martyr, whom, consecrated with the grace of the pontifical order, Saint Clement sent [sic: *dixerit*] into the Gauls, and, his preaching accomplished, for the testimony of Christ, his head dashed, he fell a victor.
